hook: David MacKay studied Natural Sciences at Trinity College, Cambridge, before completing a PhD at the California Institute of Technology in 1992 under John Hopfield, developing Bayesian methods for adaptive models. His 1992 paper 'A Practical Bayesian Framework for Backpropagation Networks' showed how Bayesian probability could be applied rigorously to neural networks, giving the field principled tools for model comparison and regularization. He returned to Cambridge, rising from Lecturer to Professor of Natural Philosophy in the Cavendish Laboratory, and in 2003 published Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms, a textbook that became a standard reference across machine learning and information theory and that he made freely available online. In 2009 he was appointed Chief Scientific Advisor to the UK Department of Energy and Climate Change, where he wrote the influential book Sustainable Energy Without the Hot Air, and in 2013 he became Cambridge's first Regius Professor of Engineering. MacKay was knighted in the 2016 New Year Honours for his services to scientific advice in government and science outreach, and he died of stomach cancer in April 2016 at the age of 48.

achievements.title: Bayesian framework for neural networks
achievements.impact: Gave neural network researchers a principled, probabilistic way to compare models, choose regularization, and estimate uncertainty, work that anticipated much of today's Bayesian deep learning.

achievements.title: Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms
achievements.impact: Wrote a free, widely used textbook connecting information theory directly to machine learning, which became a standard reference for a generation of researchers and students.

achievements.title: Dasher text entry system
achievements.impact: Developed an information efficient predictive text entry interface that gave people with motor disabilities a faster way to communicate using eye tracking or other limited input.

achievements.title: UK government science advice
achievements.impact: As Chief Scientific Advisor to the Department of Energy and Climate Change, used quantitative analysis in Sustainable Energy Without the Hot Air to shape public debate on national energy policy.
